newsitem.title: UK: Text of LME statement on copper warehouse stocks.
newsitem.headline: Text of LME statement on copper warehouse stocks.

text.p: The following is the full text of a statement issued by the London Metal Exchange (LME) regarding reports of possible large stocks outside its system:
"The London Metal Exchange has seen reports about the possible existence of large stocks of copper in Rotterdam outside its warehousing system."

"The LME has no legal jurisdiction or regulatory control over stocks maintained by producers, fabricators, merchants or others outside its warehousing system. It, therefore, cannot require such stocks to be reported to it."
"Consequently, it is unable to comment upon the existence or the extent of such stocks. Nor, indeed, is it in any position to know whether any such stocks would be of LME registered brands."

"It notes, however, that the analysis by the World Bureau of Metal Statistics emphasised that over half the total receipts by Rotterdam warehouses between 1991 and 1994 did not meet LME specifications, and could never, therefore, be counted in reported LME stocks."
"All warehouses approved by the LME are required to report regularly on a twice weekly basis the movement of all stocks entering or leaving warehouses, and the information is made public."
"All LME warehouses are regularly reminded about their obligations to comply with these requirements. Any breaches of the rules are dealt with strictly." (ends text)
